layout.hierarchy: Red title dominates at top; the 2x2 plot grid is the main visual mass; black instruction line is secondary; yellow M labels are small accents inside each subplot.

visual_elements.description: Four small MATLAB-style plots in a 2x2 grid. Each shows ~10 blue open-circle data points sampled from a green sinusoidal curve, with a red polynomial fit of increasing order. Axes: horizontal labeled 'x' (range 0 to 1), vertical labeled 't' (range approx -1 to 1 with ticks at -1, 0, 1). Top-left (M=0): red fit is a flat horizontal line near t=0.4; a large solid red dot is overlaid on the right portion of the plot. Top-right (M=1): red fit is a straight line sloping downward from upper-left to lower-right. Bottom-left (M=3): red cubic curve closely follows the green sine wave. Bottom-right (M=9): red curve oscillates wildly, passing exactly through every blue data point with large spikes between and beyond points. Each subplot has a small yellow boxed label in its upper-right corner reading 'M = 0', 'M = 1', 'M = 3', 'M = 9' respectively.

recreation_brief: 1. Set white slide background. 2. Add a light gray (#EEEEEE) header band across the top ~15% of the slide. 3. Place centered bold red (#CC0000) title text 'Data Overfit and Underfit' in the band. 4. Add a yellow (#FFFF99) circle with thin dark outline at top-right containing '16'. 5. Draw a thin red border rectangle framing the whole slide content area. 6. Below the band, left-aligned, add black text: 'The X axis is the input. The Y axis is the response.' 7. Draw a thick red-bordered rectangle in the center (~20-75% width, ~35-90% height). 8. Inside it, create a 2x2 grid of four small axes, each with x-axis labeled 'x' (0 to 1) and y-axis labeled 't' (-1 to 1). 9. In each axes plot ~10 blue open-circle markers along a sine wave, overlay a green (#00FF00) sine curve, and a red (#FF0000) polynomial fit: flat horizontal line (top-left), downward straight line (top-right), smooth cubic matching the sine (bottom-left), and a wild 9th-order curve passing through all points with large oscillations (bottom-right). 10. Add a small pale yellow boxed label in the upper-right of each subplot reading 'M = 0', 'M = 1', 'M = 3', 'M = 9'. 11. Optionally add a large solid red dot on the right side of the M=0 subplot to mimic the lecture pointer.
